transformation_rule: Six disjoint half-open bands over vs.market_cap in raw AUD -- mega >= 50e9, large [10e9, 50e9), mid [2e9, 10e9), small [300e6, 2e9), micro [50e6, 300e6), nano (0, 50e6). market_cap_tier is the same cut as a label.
business_rule: Bands are on market capitalisation in AUD, taken from market.valuation_snapshot and NOT rescaled. The `_bn` columns on the snapshot aggregates are a different quantity and carry finding 4 -- do not reconcile these bands against them.
join_condition: FROM market.companies_current AS c ON
grain: one row per asx_code
unit: booleans; market_cap_tier is one of mega/large/mid/small/micro/nano or NULL
applicability: FINDING 12. The six flags are COALESCE(..., FALSE) on columns declared NOT NULL DEFAULT false, so an unknown market cap is written as a measured false on all six, while market_cap_tier beside them returns NULL. Measured 10 Nov 2026: 641 of 2,566 rows (25.0%) carry six falses and a NULL tier. All three consumers test `= TRUE`, so no company is reported in a tier it is not in -- instead a quarter of the universe is invisible to every tier filter and nothing says so. Read market_cap_tier, which carries the distinction; never write `NOT is_mega`.

transformation_rule: Latest daily bar carried through unchanged; avg_volume_20d and the 52-week high/low come from their own laterals over the daily series; market_cap is carried from the valuation snapshot.
business_rule: Prices are UNADJUSTED close. `adjusted_close` exists on the source and is not used here: it is a total-return series (dividends reinvested) and is separately known to be stale, so a return computed from it would mix a price return with a total return. A corporate action inside the window therefore moves this value for a reason that is not a price move; the daily engine withholds across detected actions and the coverage of that detection is finding 1c. Freshness: `market.daily_prices` is the pipeline's anchor and is measured, not declared -- the window starts three days behind the table's own Sydney-date watermark, not behind the clock. A missing trading day is a continuity failure, not a fresh table with a hole.
join_condition: LEFT JOIN LATERAL (market.daily_prices) AS dp: ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1 -> the named row; WHERE asx_code = c.asx_code AND {current_source} ORDER BY time DESC LIMIT 1
grain: one row per asx_code, values as at the latest trading day
unit: AUD for prices; share count for volume; raw AUD for market_cap
applicability: price_date is the authority for how current the price is and is published on the row -- read it rather than assuming today. high_52w and low_52w are governed. Governed column: the builder's value is PROVISIONAL. `compute/engine/universe_writer.py` overwrites it last, driven by the governed registry, and assigns every governed column on every canonical row including an explicit NULL -- so 'no value this run' replaces the previous run's number instead of leaving it in place. Precedence is therefore: builder INSERT, then engine updaters, then the canonical writer. Until the canonical writer commits, `metric_states` and `compute_run_id` are NULL and `app/core/row_projection.py` fails the row closed as OUTSIDE_SNAPSHOT rather than serving it.

transformation_rule: Six disjoint half-open bands over vs.market_cap in raw AUD -- mega >= 50e9, large [10e9, 50e9), mid [2e9, 10e9), small [300e6, 2e9), micro [50e6, 300e6), nano (0, 50e6). market_cap_tier is the same cut as a label.

grain: one row per asx_code

Read market_cap_tier, which carries the distinction; never write `NOT is_mega`.

grain: one row per asx_code per named fiscal year
applicability: The prior-year lateral pins `fiscal_year = <base>.fiscal_year - N` by name rather than taking OFFSET N. OFFSET returned the previous ROW, so a company missing a year had its 'prior year' taken from two or more years back and the comparison spanned an interval nobody declared. If year N is absent the value is NULL -- unknown, not zero. A company that did not report in a named year has NULL for that year and NULL for every growth rate derived from it. The gap does not shift the series.

transformation_rule: Boolean comparisons computed inline, each under a CASE that yields NULL when either side is missing.
business_rule: Directional claims about profit quality -- margins expanding, earnings beating revenue growth. Period: the latest fiscal year the company has reported (`pnl0`, chosen by ORDER BY fiscal_year DESC LIMIT 1), NOT a fixed calendar year. Two companies in the same row of a screen may be reporting periods up to eleven months apart, and the period itself is not published on the row.
derivation_formula: CASE WHEN ym.avg_gross_margin_3y BETWEEN -100 AND 100 AND ym.avg_gross_margin_5y BETWEEN -100 AND 100 THEN ROUND((ym.avg_gross_margin_3y - ym.avg_gross_margin_5y)::numeric, 4) END AS gross_margin_expansion
join_condition: LEFT JOIN LATERAL (market.yearly_metrics) AS ym: ORDER BY fiscal_year DESC LIMIT 1 -> the named row; WHERE asx_code = c.asx_code ORDER BY fiscal_year DESC LIMIT 1
grain: one row per asx_code at the latest fiscal year
unit: booleans, and decimal ratios for the magnitudes
applicability: A NULL here is unknown, not false, and the CASE structure preserves that -- unlike market.weekly_metrics (finding 10), where the same situation is written FALSE. Governed column: the builder's value is PROVISIONAL. `compute/engine/universe_writer.py` overwrites it last, driven by the governed registry, and assigns every governed column on every canonical row including an explicit NULL -- so 'no value this run' replaces the previous run's number instead of leaving it in place. Precedence is therefore: builder INSERT, then engine updaters, then the canonical writer. Until the canonical writer commits, `metric_states` and `compute_run_id` are NULL and `app/core/row_projection.py` fails the row closed as OUTSIDE_SNAPSHOT rather than serving it. Source carries finding 6: of 188 columns on `market.yearly_metrics`, 27 are never written and 37 hold frozen values produced by the superseded `_avg` helper -- proven by window-length inversions, where avg_roe_10y exceeds avg_roe_7y on the same company. Check a column against that census before relying on it.
column_comment: avg_gross_margin_3y - avg_gross_margin_5y, in percentage points. Positive means the recent three years averaged a higher gross margin than the five year window. NULL when either average is missing.
